<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>In Our Home Business: </I>Net revenues were $3.6&nbsp;billion in 2010, a decrease of 7% compared to net revenues of $3.9&nbsp;billion in 2009. On a
geographic basis, net revenues decreased in North America, Asia and EMEA and increased in Latin America. The 7% decrease in net revenues in the Home segment is primarily attributable to a 12% decrease in net revenues of set-top boxes, reflecting:
(i)&nbsp;a 5% decrease in shipments of set-top boxes and (ii)&nbsp;a lower ASP. The decrease in net revenues of set-top boxes was partially offset by higher net revenues of video and access infrastructure equipment. </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:6%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The segment had operating earnings of $152&nbsp;million in 2010, compared to operating earnings of $11&nbsp;million in 2009. The increase
in operating earnings was primarily due to (i)&nbsp;a decrease in R&amp;D expenditures, reflecting savings from cost-reduction initiatives, (ii)&nbsp;an increase in gross margin, driven by a favorable product margin mix across product lines, and
(iii) a non-recurring charge in Other charges (income) to settle a legal matter in 2009. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Major Challenges and Accomplishments in 2010
</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In the Mobile Devices business, the wireless handset market grew in 2010 and remained intensely competitive. The growth in the market was driven
primarily by increasing demand for smartphones. To address this segment of the handset market, we focused on enhancing our smartphone portfolio. During the year, we launched 23 smartphones in markets around the world. We shipped 13.7 million
smartphones compared to two million in 2009. In addition, we launched a number of feature phones, including those based on our iDEN technology, and introduced several voice-centric devices to meet specific market requirements, primarily in emerging
markets. However, we continued to face challenges as we transitioned our product portfolio. From a financial perspective, the Mobile Devices&#146; revenues grew in 2010 compared to 2009, our first year of annual revenue growth since 2006. We also
significantly reduced our operating loss compared to 2009 by shifting our overall product mix to higher margin smartphones from lower margin feature phones, improving supply chain efficiency, and reducing operating expenses.
</FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In the Home business, weakened macro economic conditions provided some challenges for the industry. Demand for set-top boxes declined year-on-year in
the first half of the year followed by modest growth in the second half. To strengthen our product portfolio, we made a number of enhancements including advanced set-top boxes, including those which can enable viewing of 3D TV, software solutions
that allow operators to manage content across a multi-screen environment, and a multi-media IP hub that gives consumers more control and access to content. In infrastructure, revenues grew in 2010 as operators upgraded networks to expand capacity
and provide capabilities for advanced services. From a financial perspective, while Home revenues declined in 2010 compared to 2009, we improved our operating margin by remaining focused on our priority markets, introducing innovative new products,
and reducing operating expenses while continuing to invest in future growth opportunities. However, we continue to be impacted by economic conditions in the U.S. primarily as a result of the housing market. </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Looking Forward </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%;padding-bottom:0px;"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In our Mobile Devices business, while we expect the overall global mobile device market to remain intensely
competitive, we expect annual growth in total industry demand over the next several years, particularly in smartphones and media tablets. Our strategy is focused on developing and marketing a comprehensive smartphone portfolio and strengthening our
position in priority markets. Our smartphone portfolio focus will be on the following: (i)&nbsp;differentiating our products with software and services, including MOTOBLUR<FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1"><SUP
STYLE="vertical-align:baseline; position:relative; bottom:.8ex">&#153;</SUP></FONT>, our proprietary applications and services suite, (ii)&nbsp;enhancing the ecosystem using our developer network (&#147;MotoDEV&#148;) application development
program, and (iii)&nbsp;providing a smartphone portfolio across multiple price points for a broad array of carrier, distributor and retail customers. Our mid- to high-tier feature phone portfolio will be more limited given declining demand in this
segment of the handset industry. We will continue to develop and market our iDEN portfolio of devices, although we expect overall iDEN unit demand in 2011 to be lower than in 2010. For lower-priced, voice-centric mobile devices, our portfolio will
also be limited as we deliver devices to meet certain market needs. To address a new growth opportunity, we have announced a media tablet, a wireless device which enables expanded mobile Internet, content consumption, and enterprise experiences for
consumers and business users. We expect significant annual growth in total industry demand for media tablets over the next several years and for this market to be intensely competitive. Mobile Devices&#146; market priorities continue to be primarily
North America, China, and Latin America, followed by Western Europe and other strategic markets. With the growth in demand for smartphones and media tablets, and by accelerating our speed to market, providing rich consumer experiences and
strengthening our brand, we expect to continue to improve the financial performance in Mobile Devices. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In our Home business,
we expect overall industry demand in 2011 to be comparable to 2010 levels. We expect a return to industry growth when market conditions improve, particularly in the U.S., which may drive increased consumer demand for high definition TV set-top
boxes, whole-home network solutions, 3D-TV, advanced interactive services and converged experiences. In addition, consumer demand for video services is expected to drive the need for infrastructure equipment to optimize networks and storage,
increase bandwidth, and provide new services. We will continue to leverage our leadership position in set-top boxes and video delivery systems and prioritize our research and development efforts to position ourselves for future growth and emerging
market opportunities. We will also continue to manage our overall cost structure and prioritize our product portfolio to ensure we continue to operate profitably. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Other opportunities we plan to focus on include those resulting from the convergence of industries like wireless, media, computing and the Internet. These industries are increasingly interacting with each
other, which we expect will create demand for new consumer devices, applications and services. We believe we will be well positioned to deliver innovative experiences, both in the home and on the go, across multiple types of devices to address this
emerging opportunity. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">We conduct our business in highly competitive markets, facing both new and established competitors. The
markets for many of our products are characterized by rapidly changing technologies, frequent new product introductions, changing consumer trends, short product life cycles and evolving industry standards. Market disruptions caused by new
technologies, the entry of new competitors, consolidations among our customers and competitors, changes in regulatory requirements, or other factors, can introduce volatility into our businesses. We face challenging, but relatively stable, global
economic conditions with more limited visibility than historical norms. Meeting all of these challenges requires consistent operational planning and execution and investment in technology, resulting in innovative products that meet the needs of our
customers around the world. As we execute on meeting these objectives, we remain focused on taking the necessary action to design and deliver differentiated and innovative products, services and experiences that simplify, connect, and enrich
people&#146;s lives. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For more information, about our strategy and the risk related to our strategy and our future performance,
see the sections under &#147;<I>Business&#151;Business Segments</I>&#148; entitled<I> </I>&#147;<I>Mobile Devices Segment&#151;Our Strategy</I>&#148; and<I> </I>&#147;<I>Home Segment&#151;Our Strategy</I>&#148; and &#147;<I>Risk Factors</I>&#148;<I>
</I>included elsewhere in this document.<I> </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">We will operate our business differently as a new public company following the
separation from our Former Parent. For more information on the challenges and risks related to our separation from our Former Parent, see the sections entitled &#147;<I>Risk Factors&#151;Risks Relating to the Separation</I>&#148;<I> </I>and<I>
</I>&#147;<I>The Separation</I>&#148;<I> </I>in this document. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2010 Compared to Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Net Revenues </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Net revenues were $11.5 billion in 2010, up 4% compared to
net revenues of $11.1 billion in 2009. The increase in net revenues reflects a $673&nbsp;million, or 9% increase in net revenues in the Mobile Devices segment, offset by a $263 million, or 7%, decrease in net revenues in the Home segment. The 9%
increase in net revenues in the Mobile Devices segment was primarily driven by a 61% increase in average selling price (&#147;ASP&#148;), partially offset by a 32% decrease in unit shipments. The 7% decrease in net revenues in the Home segment
reflects a 12% decrease in net revenues from set-top boxes, partially offset by higher net revenues from video and access infrastructure equipment. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Gross Margin </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Gross margin was $3.0 billion, or 25.9% of net revenues in
2010, compared to $2.2 billion, or 19.5% of net revenues, in 2009. The increase in gross margin reflects: (i)&nbsp;a significant increase in the Mobile Devices segment, and (ii)&nbsp;an increase in the Home segment. The increase in gross margin in
the Mobile Devices segment was primarily driven by: (i)&nbsp;a favorable product mix, specifically due to increased volume of smartphone devices, (ii)&nbsp;lower excess inventory and other related charges in 2010 than in 2009, and (iii)&nbsp;the 9%
increase in net revenues. The increase in gross margin in the Home segment was due to a favorable product margin mix across all product lines. The increase in gross margin as a percentage of net revenues in 2010 compared to 2009 reflects an increase
in gross margin percentage in both segments. The Company&#146;s overall gross margin as a percentage of net revenues is impacted by the proportion of overall net revenues generated by its various businesses. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Selling, General and Administrative Expenses </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Selling, general and administrative (&#147;SG&amp;A&#148;) expenses increased 7% to $1.6&nbsp;billion, or 13.9% of net revenues, in 2010, compared to $1.5 billion, or 13.4% of net revenues, in 2009. The
increase in SG&amp;A expenses reflects higher SG&amp;A expenses in both segments. The increase in SG&amp;A expenses in the Mobile Devices segment was primarily driven by an increase in marketing expenses. The increase in SG&amp;A expenses in the
Home segment was primarily due to a charge to settle a legal matter. SG&amp;A expenses as a percentage of net revenues increased in the Home segment and decreased slightly in the Mobile Devices Segment. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Research and Development Expenditures </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Research and development (&#147;R&amp;D&#148;) expenditures decreased 7% to $1.5 billion, or 12.9% of net revenues, in 2010, compared to $1.6 billion, or 14.4% of net revenues, in 2009. The decrease in
R&amp;D expenditures reflects lower R&amp;D expenditures in both segments, which was primarily due to savings from cost-reduction initiatives. R&amp;D expenditures as a percentage of net revenues decreased in both segments. The Company participates
in very competitive industries with constant changes in technology and, accordingly, the Company continues to believe that a strong commitment to R&amp;D is required to drive long-term growth. </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Other Charges (Income) </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company recorded net other income of $182&nbsp;million in Other charges (income) in 2010, compared to net other charges of $287&nbsp;million in 2009. The net other income in 2010 included $283 million
of gains related to legal settlements, partially offset by: (i)&nbsp;$55 million of charges relating to the amortization of intangible assets, and (ii)&nbsp;$46 million of net reorganization of business charges included in Other charges (income).
The charges in 2009 include: (i)&nbsp;$155&nbsp;million of net reorganization of business charges included in Other charges, (ii)&nbsp;a $75 million charge related to a legal settlement, and (iii)&nbsp;$57&nbsp;million of charges relating to the
amortization of intangibles. The net reorganization of business charges are discussed in further detail in the section entitled &#147;<I>Reorganization of Businesses</I>&#148; included elsewhere in this document. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Interest Expense, Net </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Net interest expense was $52 million in 2010, compared to net interest expense of $41&nbsp;million in 2009. Net interest expense in 2010
includes interest expense of $84&nbsp;million, partially offset by interest income of $32&nbsp;million. Net interest expense in 2009 includes interest expense of $70&nbsp;million, partially offset by interest income of $29&nbsp;million. Our net
interest expense primarily represents the amount allocated from our Former Parent. This allocation is based on the Company&#146;s Total assets as a percentage of the respective Former Parent&#146;s Total assets, less Cash and cash equivalents and
Sigma Fund included in our Former Parent&#146;s consolidated balance sheets. Our interest income and interest expense as an independent, publicly traded company are expected to differ from the amounts reflected above. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Losses on Sales of Investments and Business, Net </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company had no gains (losses) on sales of investments and businesses during 2010, compared to a loss of $34 million in 2009. In 2009, the net loss primarily relates to the sale of a business in the
Mobile Devices segment. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Other </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Net expense classified as Other, as presented in Other income (expense), was $28 million in 2010, compared to $49 million in 2009. The net expense in 2010 was primarily comprised of $29 million of foreign
currency losses. The net expense in 2009 was primarily comprised of: (i)&nbsp;$45&nbsp;million of foreign currency losses and (ii)&nbsp;$11&nbsp;million of investment impairment charges. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Income Tax Expense </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company recorded $75 million of net tax expense in
2010, compared to a <I>de minimis</I> net tax expense in 2009. The Company&#146;s effective tax rates for 2010 and 2009 were less than the U.S. statutory tax rate of 35%, primarily due to no net tax benefits being recorded on the Company&#146;s 2010
and 2009 U.S. losses and certain losses in Brazil and in China due to offsetting valuation allowances. Additionally, the Company&#146;s tax provisions include net tax expense primarily related to foreign withholding taxes incurred during the period
on royalty and dividend income. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company&#146;s effective tax rate will change from period to period based on
non-recurring events, such as the settlement of tax audits, changes in valuation allowances and the tax impact of significant unusual or extraordinary items, as well as recurring factors, including changes in the geographic mix of income before
taxes, the level of pre-tax income or losses and effects of various global income tax strategies. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Net Loss </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company incurred a loss before income taxes of $4&nbsp;million in 2010, compared with a loss before income taxes of $1.3 billion in
2009. After taxes, and excluding Earnings (loss) attributable to non-controlling interests, the Company incurred a net loss of $86 million in 2010, compared to a net loss of $1.3&nbsp;billion in 2009. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The decrease in the loss before income taxes in 2010 compared to 2009 was primarily attributable to: (i)&nbsp;a $812&nbsp;million increase
in gross margin, primarily due to a favorable product mix, (ii)&nbsp;a $469 million improvement in Other charges (income), primarily due to a $283&nbsp;million gain related to legal settlements and a $109 million decrease in net reorganization of
business charges included in Other charges (income), and (iii)&nbsp;a $112 million decrease in R&amp;D expenditures. </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 Compared to Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 </I></B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Net Revenues </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Net
revenues were $11.1&nbsp;billion in 2009, down 35% compared to net revenues of $17.1&nbsp;billion in 2008. The decrease in net revenues reflects: (i)&nbsp;a $5.0&nbsp;billion, or 41%, decrease in net revenues in the Mobile Devices segment, and
(ii)&nbsp;a $1.0&nbsp;billion, or 21%, decrease in net revenues in the Home segment. The 41% decrease in net revenues in the Mobile Devices segment was primarily driven by a 45% decrease in unit shipments, partially offset by an 8% increase in ASP.
The 21% decrease in net revenues in the Home segment was primarily driven by a 24% decrease in net revenues of set-top boxes, reflecting: (i)&nbsp;an 18% decrease in unit shipments of set-top boxes, primarily due to lower shipments to large cable
and telecommunications operators in North America as a result of macroeconomic conditions, and (ii)&nbsp;a lower ASP due to an unfavorable shift in product mix. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Gross Margin </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Gross margin was $2.2&nbsp;billion, or 19.5% of net revenues,
in 2009, compared to $2.8 billion, or 16.5% of net revenues, in 2008. Gross margin decreased in both segments. The decrease in gross margin in the Mobile Devices segment was primarily driven by the 41% decrease in net revenues, partially offset by:
(i)&nbsp;supply chain efficiencies, primarily including lower excess inventory charges in 2009 than in 2008, when the charges included a $370&nbsp;million charge due to a decision to consolidate software and silicon platforms, and (ii)&nbsp;the
absence in 2009 of a comparable $150&nbsp;million charge in 2008 related to settlement of a silicon purchase commitment. The decrease in gross margin in the Home segment was primarily driven by the 21% decrease in net revenues, as there was only a
slight decline in margin percentage. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The increase in gross margin as a percentage of net revenues in 2009 compared to 2008 was
primarily driven by an increase in gross margin percentage in the Mobile Devices segment, partially offset by a slight decrease in gross margin percentage in the Home segment. The Company&#146;s overall gross margin as a percentage of net revenues
can be impacted by the proportion of overall net revenues generated by its various businesses. In 2009, the proportion of overall revenues by our Mobile Devices business was smaller than in previous years. Since Mobile Devices generally has the
lower gross margin percentage of the Company&#146;s businesses, this positively impacted overall gross margin percentage in 2009. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Selling,
General and Administrative Expenses </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">SG&amp;A expenses decreased 33% to $1.5&nbsp;billion, or 13.4% of net revenues, in
2009, compared to $2.2&nbsp;billion, or 12.9% of net revenues, in 2008. SG&amp;A expenses decreased in the Mobile Devices segment and increased in the Home segment. The decrease in SG&amp;A expenses in the Mobile Devices segment was primarily driven
by lower marketing expenses and savings from cost-reduction initiatives. The slight increase in SG&amp;A expenses in the Home segment was primarily due to increased administrative expenses, partially offset by savings from cost-reduction
initiatives. SG&amp;A expenses as a percentage of net revenues increased in both segments. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Research and Development Expenditures
</I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">R&amp;D expenditures decreased 32% to $1.6&nbsp;billion, or 14.4% of net revenues, in 2009, compared to $2.4&nbsp;billion,
or 13.8% of net revenues, in 2008. R&amp;D expenditures decreased in both segments, primarily due to savings from cost-reduction initiatives. R&amp;D expenditures as a percentage of net revenues increased in both segments. The Company participates
in very competitive industries with constant changes in technology and, accordingly, the Company continues to believe that a strong commitment to R&amp;D is required to drive long-term growth. </FONT></P>

charges, (ii)&nbsp;a $75 million charge related to a legal settlement, and (iii)&nbsp;$57&nbsp;million of charges relating to the amortization of intangibles. The net charges in 2008 included: (i)&nbsp;$151&nbsp;million of net reorganization of
business charges included in Other charges, (ii)&nbsp;$64&nbsp;million of charges relating to the amortization of intangible assets, and (iii)&nbsp;$68 million of goodwill and other asset impairment charges. The net reorganization of business

<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Interest Income (Expense), Net </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT

by interest income of $29&nbsp;million. Net interest income in 2008 included interest income of $99&nbsp;million, partially offset by interest expense of $71&nbsp;million. Our interest expense primarily represents the amount allocated from our
Former Parent. This allocation is based on the Company&#146;s Total assets as a percentage of the respective Former Parent&#146;s Total assets, less Cash and cash equivalents and Sigma Fund included in our Former Parent&#146;s consolidated balance
sheets. Our interest expense as an independent, stand-alone company will differ from the amounts reflected above. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Gains (Losses) on Sales

gains of $11&nbsp;million in 2008. In 2009, the net losses primarily relate to the sale of a business. In 2008, the net gains primarily related to sales of a number of the Company&#146;s equity investments. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Other, net </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Net expense
classified as Other, as presented in Other income (expense), was $49&nbsp;million in 2009, compared to net income of $64&nbsp;million in 2008. The net expense in 2009 was primarily comprised of: (i)&nbsp;$45&nbsp;million of foreign currency losses
and (ii)&nbsp;$11&nbsp;million of investment impairment charges. The net income in 2008 was primarily comprised of: (i)&nbsp;a $99&nbsp;million curtailment gain associated with the decision to freeze benefit accruals for U.S. pension plans, and
(ii)&nbsp;$56&nbsp;million of gains related to the extinguishment of a liability, partially offset by: (i)&nbsp;$67&nbsp;million of foreign currency losses, and (ii)&nbsp;$36&nbsp;million of investment impairment charges. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Income Tax Expense </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The
Company recorded a <I>de minimis</I> net tax expense in 2009, compared to $1.0 billion of net tax expense in 2008. The Company&#146;s effective tax rate in 2009 was less than the U.S. statutory tax rate of 35% primarily due to no net U.S. tax
benefits being recorded on the Company&#146;s U.S. losses due to the inability to recognize additional deferred tax assets. The Company&#146;s effective tax rate in 2008 was less than the U.S. statutory tax rate of 35% primarily due to the recording
of a $2.0 billion non-cash tax charge to establish full valuation allowances against the Company&#146;s U.S., Brazil and China deferred tax assets, partially offset by a net reduction in unrecognized tax benefits. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company&#146;s effective tax rate will change from period to period based on non-recurring events, such as the settlement of tax
audits, changes in valuation allowances and the tax impact of significant unusual or extraordinary items, as well as recurring factors including changes in the geographic mix of income before taxes, the level of pre-tax income or losses and effects
of various global income tax strategies. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Net Loss </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company incurred a loss before income taxes of $1.3&nbsp;billion in 2009, compared with a loss before income taxes of $1.9&nbsp;billion in 2008. After taxes, and excluding Earnings (losses)
attributable to non-controlling interests, the Company incurred a net loss of $1.3&nbsp;billion in 2009, compared to a net loss of $3.0&nbsp;billion in 2008. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The improvement in the loss before income taxes in 2009 compared to 2008 was primarily attributable to: (i)&nbsp;a $767&nbsp;million decrease in R&amp;D expenditures, and (ii)&nbsp;a $732&nbsp;million
decrease in SG&amp;A expenses. These factors were partially offset by a $666&nbsp;million decrease in gross margin. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Segment Results

<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2010 Compared to Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 </I></B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 2010, the segment&#146;s net revenues were $7.8 billion, an increase of 9% compared to net revenues of $7.1 billion in 2009. The 9%
increase in net revenues was primarily driven by a 61% increase in average selling price (&#147;ASP&#148;), partially offset by a 32% decrease in unit shipments. The segment&#146;s unit shipments reflected a decreased focus on the feature phone and
voice-centric device segments of the market partially offset by higher unit shipments of smartphones. On a geographic basis, net revenues increased in North America, Asia and the Europe, Middle East and Africa region (&#147;EMEA&#148;), partially
offset by decreased net revenues in Latin America. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The segment incurred an operating loss of $76 million in 2010, compared to
an operating loss of $1.2 billion in 2009. The decrease in the operating loss was primarily due to an increase in gross margin driven by: (i)&nbsp;a favorable product mix, specifically due to increased volume of smartphone devices, (ii)&nbsp;lower
excess inventory and other related charges in 2010 than in 2009, and (iii)&nbsp;the 9% increase in net revenues. Also contributing to the decrease in the operating loss were: (i)&nbsp;$283&nbsp;million of gains related to legal settlements,
(ii)&nbsp;lower reorganization of business charges, and (iii)&nbsp;lower research and development (&#147;R&amp;D&#148;) expenditures, reflecting savings from cost-reduction initiatives, partially offset by higher selling, general and administrative
(&#147;SG&amp;A&#148;) expenses. As a percentage of net revenues in 2010 as compared to 2009, gross margin increased, expenses for SG&amp;A decreased slightly and R&amp;D expenditures decreased. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The segment&#146;s industry typically experiences short life cycles for new products. Therefore, it is vital to the segment&#146;s success
that new, compelling products are continually introduced. Accordingly, a strong commitment to R&amp;D is required and, even amidst challenging global economic conditions, the segment expects to continue to make the appropriate investments to develop
a differentiated product portfolio and fuel long-term growth. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The segment&#146;s backlog (excluding any deferred revenue) was
$678&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31, 2010, compared to $409&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31, 2009. This increase in backlog is primarily due to an increase in orders in North America, particularly for smartphones. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Unit shipments in 2010 were 37.3&nbsp;million units, a 32% decrease compared to shipments of 55.1&nbsp;million units in 2009. Smartphone
shipments in 2010 were 13.7&nbsp;million units. For the full year 2010, unit shipments decreased substantially in North America, Latin America and Asia and, were flat in EMEA. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 2010, ASP increased approximately 61% compared to 2009 driven by favorable product mix towards smartphones. ASP is impacted by numerous factors, including product mix, market conditions and competitive
product offerings, and ASP trends often vary over time. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The segment has several large customers located throughout the world.
In 2010, aggregate net revenues to the segment&#146;s five largest customers accounted for approximately 57% of the segment&#146;s net revenues. Besides selling directly to carriers and operators, the segment also sells products through a variety of
third-party distributors and retailers, which account for approximately 21% of the segment&#146;s net revenues in 2010. The loss of any of the segment&#146;s key customers could have a significant impact on the segment&#146;s business. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-bottom:0px; margin-top:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">53</FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:3px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:1px" align="left"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P></TD></TR>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Although the U.S. market continued to be the segment&#146;s largest individual market, many
of our customers, and 36% of the segment&#146;s 2010 net revenues, were outside the U.S. In 2010, the largest of these international markets were China, Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Korea. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 Compared to Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 2009, the segment&#146;s net revenues were $7.1&nbsp;billion, a decrease of 41% compared to net revenues of $12.2&nbsp;billion in 2008. The segment&#146;s net revenues were negatively impacted by
reduced product offerings in large market segments, particularly 3G products, including smartphones, and the segment&#146;s limited product offerings in very low-tier products. The 41% decrease in net revenues was primarily driven by a 45% decrease
in unit shipments, partially offset by an 8% increase in ASP. On a geographic basis, net revenues decreased substantially in Latin America, EMEA and Asia and, to a lesser extent, decreased in North America. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The segment incurred an operating loss of $1.2&nbsp;billion in 2009, an improvement of 49% compared to an operating loss of
$2.4&nbsp;billion in 2008. The decrease in the operating loss was primarily due to decreases in: (i)&nbsp;SG&amp;A expenses, primarily due to lower marketing expenses and savings from cost-reduction initiatives, (ii)&nbsp;R&amp;D expenditures,
reflecting savings from cost-reduction initiatives, (iii)&nbsp;supply chain efficiencies, primarily including lower excess inventory charges in 2009 than in 2008, when the charges included a $370&nbsp;million charge due to a decision to consolidate
software and silicon platforms, and (iv)&nbsp;the absence in 2009 of a comparable $150&nbsp;million charge in 2008 related to settlement of a silicon purchase commitment, partially offset by a decrease in gross margin, driven by the 41% decrease in
net revenues. As a percentage of net revenues in 2009 as compared to 2008, gross margin, SG&amp;A expenses and R&amp;D expenditures all increased. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The segment&#146;s industry typically experiences short life cycles for new products. Therefore, it is vital to the segment&#146;s success that new, compelling products are continually introduced.
Accordingly, a strong commitment to R&amp;D is required and, even amidst challenging global economic conditions, the segment expects to continue to make the appropriate investments to develop a differentiated product portfolio and fuel long-term
growth. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The segment&#146;s backlog (excluding any deferred revenue) was $409&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31, 2009, compared
to $290&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31, 2008. This increase in backlog is primarily due to an increase in orders in North America, particularly for 3G products, including smartphones. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Unit shipments in 2009 were 55.1&nbsp;million units, a 45% decrease compared to shipments of 100.1&nbsp;million units in 2008. For the
full year 2009, unit shipments decreased substantially in Latin America, EMEA and Asia and, to a lesser extent, decreased in North America. While the total unit shipments in the worldwide mobile device market decreased by approximately 6% in 2009,
unit shipments by the segment decreased by a significantly higher percentage than the overall market. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 2009, ASP increased
approximately 8% compared to 2008. The overall increase in ASP was driven primarily by changes in the product tier and geographic mix of revenues, particularly in the fourth quarter of 2009 when the segment shipped approximately two million
Android-powered smartphones. By comparison, ASP was flat in 2008. ASP is impacted by numerous factors, including product mix, geographic mix, market conditions and competitive product offerings, and ASP trends often vary over time. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The segment has several large customers located throughout the world. In 2009, aggregate net revenues to the segment&#146;s five largest
customers accounted for approximately 54% of the segment&#146;s net revenues. Besides selling directly to carriers and operators, the segment also sells products through a variety of third-party distributors and retailers, which account for
approximately 21% of the segment&#146;s net revenues in 2009. The loss of any of the segment&#146;s key customers could have a significant impact on the segment&#146;s business. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Although the U.S. market continued to be the segment&#146;s largest individual market, many of our customers, and 42% of the
segment&#146;s 2009 net revenues, were outside the U.S. In 2009, the largest of these international markets were Brazil, China, Mexico and Korea. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Home Segment </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Home segment designs, manufactures, sells,
installs and services&nbsp;set-top boxes for digital video, IP video, satellite and terrestrial broadcast networks, end-to-end digital video and IPTV distribution systems, broadband </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2010 Compared to Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 </I></B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 2010, the segment&#146;s net revenues were $3.6 billion, a decrease of 7% compared to net revenues of $3.9 billion in 2009. The 7%
decrease in net revenues in the Home segment is primarily attributable to a 12% decrease in net revenues from set-top boxes, reflecting: (i)&nbsp;a 5% decrease in shipments of set-top boxes and (ii)&nbsp;a lower ASP. The decrease in net revenues
from set-top boxes was partially offset by higher net revenues from video and access infrastructure equipment. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Shipments of SD
set-top boxes decreased significantly, primarily due to lower shipments to large telecommunication and cable operators in North America as a result of lower demand. The decrease in unit shipments of SD set-top boxes was partially offset by an
increase in unit shipments of HD and HD/digital video recording (together, &#147;HD/DVR&#148;) set-top boxes due to increased demand for HD and DVR capabilities. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On a geographic basis, net revenues decreased in North America, Asia and EMEA and increased in Latin America. Net revenues in North America continued to comprise a significant portion of the
segment&#146;s business, accounting for approximately 75% of the segment&#146;s net revenues in 2010, compared to approximately 78% in 2009. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The segment had operating earnings of $152 million in 2010, compared to operating earnings of $11 million in 2009. The increase in operating earnings was primarily due to (i)&nbsp;a decrease in R&amp;D
expenditures, reflecting savings from cost-reduction initiatives, (ii)&nbsp;an increase in gross margin, driven by a favorable product margin mix across product lines and (iii)&nbsp;a $75 million non-recurring charge to settle a legal matter during
2009. As a percentage of net revenues in 2010 as compared to 2009, gross margin and SG&amp;A expenses increased while R&amp;D expenditures decreased. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The segment is dependent upon a small number of customers for a significant portion of its revenues. In 2010, revenues to the segment&#146;s top five customers represented approximately 48% of the
segment&#146;s net revenues. The loss of one of these major customers could have a significant impact on the segment&#146;s business. The segment&#146;s backlog was $432&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31, 2010, compared to $378&nbsp;million at
December&nbsp;31, 2009. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In the Home business, demand for the segment&#146;s products depends primarily on the level of
spending by cable and telecommunication customers for their service offerings, including construction or expansion of their communications systems. In 2010, demand for our digital video products decreased in North&nbsp;America due to difficult
macroeconomic conditions that led to reduced capital expenditures. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 Compared to Year Ended
December&nbsp;31, 2008 </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 2009, the segment&#146;s net revenues were $3.9&nbsp;billion, a decrease of 21% compared to
net revenues of $4.9&nbsp;billion in 2008. The 21% decrease in net revenues in the Home business was primarily driven by: (i)&nbsp;an 18% decrease in shipments of set-top boxes, primarily due to lower shipments to large cable and telecommunications
operators in North America as a result of macroeconomic conditions, and (ii)&nbsp;a lower ASP due to an unfavorable shift in product mix. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Net revenues from SD set-top boxes and HD set-top boxes decreased significantly, primarily due to lower shipments to large telecommunication and cable operators in North America as a result of lower
demand. The decrease in unit shipments of SD and HD set-top boxes was partially offset by (i)&nbsp;an increase in HD/DVR units shipments due to increased demand for DVR capabilities, and (ii)&nbsp;an increase in IP based set-top boxes. </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On a geographic basis, the 21% decrease in net revenues was primarily driven by lower net

STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Reorganization of Businesses </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Prior to the separation, the Company
participated in our Former Parent&#146;s formal Involuntary Severance Plan (&#147;Severance Plan&#148;), which permits the Company to offer eligible employees severance benefits based on years of service and employment grade level in the event that
employment is involuntarily terminated as a result of a reduction-in-force or restructuring. Effective August&nbsp;1, 2009, our Former Parent amended and restated the Severance Plan. Under the amended Severance Plan, severance benefits will be paid
in biweekly installments to impacted employees rather than in lump sum payments. The Company recognizes termination benefits based on formulas per the Severance Plan at the point in time that future settlement is probable and can be reasonably
estimated based on estimates prepared at the time a restructuring plan is approved by management. Exit costs consist of future minimum lease payments on vacated facilities and other contractual terminations. At each reporting date, the Company
evaluates its accruals for employee separation and exit costs to ensure the accruals are still appropriate. In certain circumstances, accruals are no longer needed because of efficiencies in carrying out the plans or because employees previously
identified for separation resigned from the Company and did not receive severance or were redeployed due to circumstances not foreseen when the original plans were initiated. In these cases, the Company reverses accruals through the combined
statements of operations where the original charges were recorded when it is determined they are no longer needed. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company
realized cost-saving benefits of approximately $46&nbsp;million in 2010 from the plans that were initiated during 2010, representing: (i)&nbsp;$30&nbsp;million of savings in R&amp;D expenditures, (ii)&nbsp;$9&nbsp;million of savings in SG&amp;A
expenses, and (iii)&nbsp;$7&nbsp;million of savings in Costs of sales. Beyond 2010, the Company expects the reorganization plans initiated during 2010 to provide annualized cost savings of approximately $143&nbsp;million, representing:
(i)&nbsp;$72&nbsp;million of savings in R&amp;D expenditures, (ii)&nbsp;$45&nbsp;million of savings in SG&amp;A expenses, and (iii)&nbsp;$26&nbsp;million of savings in Cost of sales. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>2010 Charges </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2010, the Company continued to implement various
productivity improvement plans aimed at achieving long-term, sustainable profitability by driving efficiencies and reducing operating costs. Both of the Company&#146;s business segments were impacted by these plans. The employees affected were
located in all regions. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2010, the Company recorded net reorganization of business charges of $63&nbsp;million,
including $17&nbsp;million of charges in Costs of sales and $46&nbsp;million of charges under Other charges in the Company&#146;s combined statements of operations. Included in the aggregate $63&nbsp;million are charges of $81&nbsp;million for
employee separation costs, partially offset by $18&nbsp;million of reversals for accruals no longer needed. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Exit Costs </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">At
January&nbsp;1, 2010, the Company had an accrual of $39&nbsp;million for exit costs attributable to lease terminations. There were no material additional charges related to exit costs during 2010. The adjustments of $7&nbsp;million reflect:
(i)&nbsp;$6 million of reversals of accruals no longer needed, and (ii)&nbsp;$1 million of foreign currency translation adjustments. The $20&nbsp;million used reflects cash payments. The remaining accrual of $12&nbsp;million, which is included in
Accrued liabilities in the Company&#146;s combined balance sheet at December&nbsp;31, 2010, represents future cash payments, primarily for lease termination obligations that are expected to be paid over a number of years. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Employee Separation Costs </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">At January&nbsp;1, 2010, the Company had an accrual of $33&nbsp;million for employee separation costs, representing the severance costs
for approximately 400 employees. The additional 2010 charges of $81&nbsp;million represent severance costs for approximately an additional 2,200 employees, of which 900 were direct employees and 1,300 were indirect employees. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The adjustments of $14&nbsp;million reflect: (i)&nbsp;$12 million of reversals of accruals no longer needed and (ii)&nbsp;$2 million of
foreign currency translation adjustments. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2010, approximately 1,500 employees, of which 500 were direct employees and
1,000 were indirect employees, were separated from the Company. The $68&nbsp;million used in 2010 reflects cash payments to these separated employees. The remaining accrual of $32&nbsp;million, which is included in Accrued liabilities in the
Company&#146;s combined balance sheet at December&nbsp;31, 2010, is expected to be paid in 2011 to: (i)&nbsp;severed employees who began receiving payments in 2010, and (ii)&nbsp;approximately 1,100 employees who will begin receiving payments in
2011. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>2009 Charges </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2009, in light of the macroeconomic decline that adversely affected revenues, the Company continued to implement various productivity improvement plans aimed at achieving long-term, sustainable
profitability by driving efficiencies and reducing operating costs. Both of the Company&#146;s business segments were impacted by these plans, with the majority of the impact in the Mobile Devices segment. The employees affected are located in all
geographic regions. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2009, the Company recorded net reorganization of business charges of $210 million, including
$55&nbsp;million of charges in Costs of sales and $155 million of charges under Other charges in the Company&#146;s combined statements of operations. Included in the aggregate $210 million are charges of $206&nbsp;million for employee separation
costs, $28&nbsp;million for exit costs and $20&nbsp;million for fixed asset impairment charges, partially offset by $44 million of reversals for accruals no longer needed. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Exit Costs </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">At
January&nbsp;1, 2009, the Company had an accrual of $63&nbsp;million for exit costs attributable to lease terminations. The additional 2009 charges of $28&nbsp;million are primarily related to the exit of leased facilities and contractual
termination costs. The adjustments of $8&nbsp;million reflect&nbsp;$9&nbsp;million of reversals of accruals no longer needed, partially offset by $1&nbsp;million of foreign currency translation adjustments. The $44&nbsp;million used in 2009 reflects
cash payments. The remaining accrual of $39&nbsp;million, which is included in Accrued liabilities in the Company&#146;s combined balance sheet at December&nbsp;31, 2009, represents future cash payments, primarily for lease termination obligations
that are expected to be paid over a number of years. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Employee Separation Costs </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">At January&nbsp;1, 2009, the Company had an accrual of $103&nbsp;million for employee separation costs, representing the severance costs
for approximately 1,600 employees. The additional 2009 charges of $206&nbsp;million represent severance costs for approximately an additional 6,300 employees, of which 2,600 were direct employees and 3,700 were indirect employees. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The adjustments of $32&nbsp;million reflect $35&nbsp;million of reversals of accruals no longer needed, partially offset by
$3&nbsp;million of foreign currency translation adjustments. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2009, approximately 7,600 employees, of which 3,500 were
direct employees and 4,100 were indirect employees, were separated from the Company. The $244&nbsp;million used in 2009 reflects cash payments to these separated employees. The remaining accrual of $33&nbsp;million was included in Accrued
liabilities in the Company&#146;s combined balance sheet at December&nbsp;31, 2009. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>2008 Charges </I></B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2008, the Company implemented various productivity improvement plans aimed at achieving long-term, sustainable profitability by
driving efficiencies and reducing operating costs. Both of the Company&#146;s business segments were impacted by these plans, with the majority of the impact in the Mobile Devices segment. The employees affected were located in all regions.
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2008, the Company recorded net reorganization of business charges of $229&nbsp;million, including $78&nbsp;million of
charges in Costs of sales and $151&nbsp;million of charges under Other charges in the Company&#146;s combined statements of operations. Included in the aggregate $229&nbsp;million were charges of $195&nbsp;million for employee separation costs,
$65&nbsp;million for exit costs and $3&nbsp;million for fixed asset impairment charges, partially offset by $34&nbsp;million of reversals for accruals no longer needed. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Exit Costs </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">At
January&nbsp;1, 2008, the Company had an accrual of $1&nbsp;million for exit costs attributable to lease terminations. The 2008 additional charges of $65&nbsp;million were primarily related to: (i)&nbsp;the exit of leased facilities in the United
Kingdom by the Mobile Devices segment, and (ii)&nbsp;the exit of leased facilities in Mexico by the Home segment. The adjustments of $2&nbsp;million primarily reflect foreign currency translation adjustments. The $5&nbsp;million used in 2008
reflects cash payments. The remaining accrual of $63&nbsp;million, which was included in Accrued liabilities in the Company&#146;s combined balance sheet at December&nbsp;31, 2008, represents future cash payments, primarily for lease termination
obligations, that are expected to be paid over a number of years. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Employee Separation Costs </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">At January&nbsp;1, 2008, the Company had an accrual of $102&nbsp;million for employee separation costs, representing the severance costs
for approximately 1,400&nbsp;employees. The additional 2008 charges of $195 million represent severance costs for approximately an additional 4,600&nbsp;employees, of which 2,200 were direct employees and 2,400 were indirect employees. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The adjustments of $33&nbsp;million reflect $34&nbsp;million of reversals of accruals no longer needed, partially offset by
$1&nbsp;million of foreign currency translation adjustments. The $34&nbsp;million of reversals represent previously accrued costs for approximately 300 employees. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2008, approximately 4,100 employees, of which 2,200 were direct employees and 1,900 were indirect employees, were separated from the Company. The $161&nbsp;million used in 2008 reflects cash
payments to these separated employees. The remaining accrual of $103 million was included in Accrued liabilities in the Company&#146;s combined balance sheet at December&nbsp;31, 2008. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Liquidity and Capital Resources </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Overview of Liquidity </I></B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">At the time of the Distribution on January&nbsp;4, 2011, our Former Parent contributed $3.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents to the
Company (the &#147;Distribution Date Contribution&#148;). An additional contribution of $300 million from our Former Parent is expected to be paid in cash if and when our Former Parent receives cash distributions as a result of the reduction in
registered capital of an overseas subsidiary (the &#147;Deferred Contribution&#148;). Our Former Parent has notified us that they have not yet received such cash distributions and do not currently know when the distribution will be complete. As an
independent, publicy traded company, we expect to fund our ongoing operations, working capital, capital expenditures and strategic investments through cash flows from operations, and our available cash and cash equivalents. We expect to invest our
cash primarily in short-term government, agency and government-sponsored enterprise obligations, diversified short-term bank deposits and money market funds. </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Credit Facilities </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On January&nbsp;4, 2011, the Company entered into a $500 million unsecured three-year credit agreement (the &#147;Credit Agreement&#148;) with a syndicate of lenders. The Credit Agreement provides for a
revolving credit facility and a letter of credit facility, is guaranteed by certain of the Company&#146;s subsidiaries, and contains restrictive covenants. The Company may use any borrowings under the Credit Agreement for general corporate purposes.
No obligations are outstanding under the Credit Agreement on the date hereof. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Our ability to obtain standby letters of credit,
performance bonds, surety bonds (collectively referred to as &#147;Letters of Credit&#148;), credit&nbsp;facilities, and foreign exchange lines primarily depends upon our capitalization, working capital, past performance, management expertise and
reputation, and certain external factors, including the condition of the capital markets, the overall capacity of Letters of Credit and foreign exchange markets. Financial institutions providing these instruments consider such factors in
relationship to their underwriting/credit standards, which may change from time to time. As an independent, publicly traded company, it may be more difficult and more costly for us to obtain such instruments. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Cash and Cash Equivalents </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Our Former Parent primarily uses a worldwide, centralized approach to cash management in which cash accounts are principally consolidated on a daily basis. Until separation, the Company participated in
this program. Therefore, the financing of the Company&#146;s operations and the related activity between the Company and our Former Parent is reflected as Net transfers from (to) Motorola, Inc. in our combined statements of business equity and of
cash flows. As a result, the Company has recorded no cash or cash equivalents on its combined balance sheets. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">At the time of
the Distribution, approximately one-third of the Company&#146;s cash and cash equivalents was held by the Company or its subsidiaries in countries outside the U.S. Approximately 80% of the Company&#146;s cash and cash equivalents were denominated in
U.S. dollars. We also have approximately $160 million of cash deposits, which is included in the $3.2 billion of cash and cash equivalents received from our Former Parent, primarily related to various legal disputes. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">As highlighted in the combined statements of cash flows, the Company&#146;s liquidity and available capital resources are impacted by
three key components: (i)&nbsp;operating activities, (ii)&nbsp;investing activities, and (iii)&nbsp;financing activities. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Operating
Activities </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The net cash generated from operating activities in 2010 was $606&nbsp;million, compared to
$1.1&nbsp;billion of cash used for operating activities in 2009 and $1.2&nbsp;billion used in 2008. The primary contributors to the net cash generation in 2010 were: (i)&nbsp;an $629&nbsp;million increase in accounts payable and accrued liabilities,
and (ii)&nbsp;net earnings (adjusted for non-cash items) of $283&nbsp;million, which included the receipt of $230 million in cash related to legal settlements, partially offset by: (i)&nbsp;a $228&nbsp;million increase in net accounts receivable,
and (ii)&nbsp;a $154 million increase in net inventories. The primary contributors to net cash used for operating activities in 2009 were: (i)&nbsp;a $1.4 billion decrease in accounts payable and accrued liabilities, and (ii)&nbsp;the net loss
(adjusted for non-cash items) of $933&nbsp;million, partially offset by: (i)&nbsp;a $1.2&nbsp;billion decrease in net inventories, and (ii)&nbsp;a $102 million net decrease in other assets and liabilities. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Accounts Receivable:</I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#146;s net accounts receivable were $1.6 billion at December&nbsp;31, 2010,
compared to $1.3&nbsp;billion at December&nbsp;31, 2009. Compared to December&nbsp;31, 2009, net accounts receivable at December&nbsp;31, 2010 were higher in both segments. The Company&#146;s businesses sell their products in a variety of markets
throughout the world and payment terms can vary by market type and geographic location. Accordingly, the Company&#146;s levels of net accounts receivable can be impacted by the timing and level of sales that are made by its various businesses and by
the geographic locations in which those sales are made. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">As further described below under <I>&#147;Sales of
Receivables,&#148;</I> from time to time, our Former Parent elects to sell accounts receivable to third-parties; until separation the Company&#146;s accounts receivable were sold in this program. The Company&#146;s levels of net accounts receivable
can be impacted by the timing and amount of such sales, which can vary by period and can be impacted by numerous factors. </FONT></P>

STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Lease obligations:</I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our Former Parent owns many of its major facilities and leases certain office, factory and warehouse space, land, and information technology and other
equipment under principally non-cancelable operating leases. Our Former Parent identifies a landlord for each facility based on the primary resident of the facility. Our Former Parent allocates a portion of its facility and lease expenses to the
Company based on the square footage occupied by employees of the Company; such allocation is included in the Company&#146;s combined statements of operations. At December&nbsp;31, 2010, future minimum lease obligations, primarily comprised of
obligations for facilities in which the Company was deemed to be the primary resident, net of minimum sublease rentals, totaled $212&nbsp;million. Total rental expense, primarily comprised of facilities rental expense, net of sublease income, was
$61&nbsp;million in 2010, $62&nbsp;million in 2009 and $72&nbsp;million in 2008. After separation, the Company occupies facilities where our Former Parent is the landlord, and our Former Parent occupies facilities where the Company is the landlord.
The Company does not expect the incremental lease expense, net of sublease income, to be materially different from the amounts recorded in the historical combined financial statements, which include amounts allocated to the Company from our Former
Parent. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Purchase obligations:</I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has entered into agreements for the purchase of
inventory, license of software, promotional activities, and research and development, which are firm commitments and are not cancelable. At December&nbsp;31, 2010, substantially all of the Company&#146;s obligations in connection with these
agreements run through 2014, and the payments expected to be made under these agreements total $510 million during that period. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company enters into a number of arrangements for the sourcing of supplies and materials with take-or-pay obligations. The
Company&#146;s obligations with these suppliers run through 2013 and total a minimum purchase obligation of $123 million during that period, which are included within purchase obligations. The Company does not anticipate the cancellation of any of
these agreements in the future and estimates that purchases from these suppliers will exceed the minimum obligations during the agreement periods. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Tax obligations:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</I>The Company has approximately $101 million of unrecognized tax benefits relating to multiple tax jurisdictions and tax years. Based on the potential outcome
of the Company&#146;s global tax examinations, the expiration of the statute of limitations for specific jurisdictions, or the continued ability to satisfy tax incentive obligations, it is reasonably possible that the unrecognized tax benefits will
change within the next 12 months. The associated net tax impact on the reserve balance is estimated to be in the range of a $0 to $50 million decrease, with cash payments in the range of $0 to $70 million. <I> </I></FONT></P>

purchase software, components, supplies and materials from suppliers. Generally, these agreements </FONT></P>

Excess of Underlying Contract Value:</I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In certain circumstances, our businesses may enter into contracts with customers pursuant to which the damages that could be claimed by the other party for failed performance might
exceed the revenue Motorola Mobility receives from the contract. Contracts with these types of uncapped damage provisions are fairly rare, but individual contracts could still represent meaningful risk. There is a possibility that a damage claim by
a counterparty to one of these contracts could result in expenses to Motorola Mobility that are far in excess of the revenue received from the counterparty in connection with the contract. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Indemnification Provisions:</I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, Motorola Mobility may provide indemnifications for losses that
result from the breach of general warranties contained in certain commercial, intellectual property and divestiture agreements. Historically, Motorola Mobility has not made significant payments under these agreements, nor have there been significant
claims asserted against Motorola Mobility. However, there is an increasing risk in relation to intellectual property indemnities given the current legal climate. In indemnification cases, payment by Motorola Mobility is conditioned on the other
party making a claim pursuant to the procedures specified in the particular contract, which procedures typically allow Motorola Mobility to challenge the other party&#146;s claims. Further, Motorola Mobility&#146;s obligations under these agreements
for indemnification based on breach of representations and warranties are generally limited in terms of duration, typically not more than 24&nbsp;months, and for amounts not in excess of the contract value, except with respect to certain
intellectual property infringement claims, and in some instances Motorola Mobility may have recourse against third-parties for certain payments made by Motorola Mobility. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT

management, the ultimate disposition of these matters is not expected to have a material adverse effect on Motorola Mobility&#146;s combined financial position, liquidity or results of operations. However, an unfavorable resolution could have a
material adverse effect on the Company&#146;s combined financial position, liquidity or results of operations in the periods in which the matters are ultimately resolved. See &#147;<I>Item 3. Legal Proceedings</I>&#148; for more details. </FONT></P>

<TD VALIGN="top" ROWSPAN="2" NOWRAP STYLE="BORDER:1px solid #000000; padding-left:8px" BGCOLOR="#e5e5e5"> <P STYLE="font-size:1px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT
